recipes.title: Brown Butter Garlic Spaghetti
recipes.summary: A weeknight pasta that tastes like you spent way more on it than you did. Brown the butter past blonde — the nutty toast is the whole point.
recipes.prefaceNote: Start the pasta water before you do anything else — it's always the bottleneck.

ingredients.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated, plus more to finish

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti to one minute shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, melt butter in a wide skillet over medium heat. Swirl often until the milk solids turn deep amber and the butter smells nutty, 4–6 minutes.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 60 seconds, until garlic is fragrant but not browned.
Off heat, add 1/2 cup pasta water to the skillet — it will hiss and emulsify. Return to low heat.
Add drained pasta and toss for 60 seconds, splashing in more pasta water as needed until the sauce coats every strand glossily.
Off heat, sprinkle in Parmigiano in two additions, tossing between each. Finish with parsley, lemon zest, a crack of black pepper, and more cheese at the table.

recipes.title: Coconut Lentil Soup
recipes.summary: A 30-minute red lentil soup with coconut milk, ginger, and turmeric. Vegan, freezer-friendly, and somehow still comforting.

ingredients.name: cilantro and chili crisp to finish

steps.text: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium. Cook onion with a pinch of salt until soft and translucent, 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and red pepper flakes. Stir 60 seconds until fragrant.
Add lentils, coconut milk, and broth. Bring to a low boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until lentils break down and the soup thickens, 18–22 minutes.
Off heat, stir in lime juice. Taste — adjust salt aggressively; coconut milk dulls it.
Ladle into bowls. Top with cilantro and a spoon of chili crisp.

recipes.title: Crunchy Apple Walnut Salad
recipes.summary: Cold, crisp, and assertive. Maple-mustard dressing carries the whole thing — make double and keep it in the fridge.

ingredients.name: crisp apples (Honeycrisp or Pink Lady), thinly sliced

steps.text: Toast walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking often, until fragrant and just darkened, 3–5 minutes. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, and maple syrup in a small jar or bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice apples last so they don't brown. A mandoline gets them paper-thin; a sharp knife is fine.
In a wide bowl, toss greens with half the dressing. Add apples, walnuts, cranberries, and cheese. Drizzle with the rest.
Serve immediately — this one does not hold.

recipes.title: Olive Oil Banana Bread
recipes.summary: Olive oil instead of butter — moister crumb, longer shelf life, and a faint fruity note that makes it taste expensive.
recipes.prefaceNote: Use bananas with black skin. If they're just yellow, the bread will taste flat.

steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a 9x5 in (23x13 cm) loaf pan with parchment, leaving overhang on the long sides.
Mash bananas in a large bowl until almost smooth — a few small lumps are fine.
Whisk in olive oil, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla. The mixture should look glossy.
In a separate bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon. Add to the wet mix and fold with a spatula until just combined. Stop when no streaks of flour remain — overmixing toughens the crumb.
Fold in walnuts if using. Scrape into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake 50–60 minutes, until a skewer in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then lift out by the parchment and cool fully on a rack before slicing.

recipes.epilogueNote: Wrapped tight, this keeps 4 days at room temperature or 3 months frozen. Slice before freezing.

recipes.title: Black Pepper Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: A weeknight stir-fry that gets its punch from a coarse pepper crust and a fast hot pan. The beef rests in cornstarch — that's the trick.
recipes.prefaceNote: Have every ingredient prepped before you turn the burner on. Stir-fry is the wrong place to multitask.

ingredients.name: flank or sirloin steak, sliced 1/4 in (0.5 cm) thick against the grain

steps.text: Toss sliced beef with cornstarch, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Rest 15 minutes at room temperature.
Stir the sauce: oyster sauce, dark soy, sugar, water. Set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or wide skillet over high heat until just smoking. Add beef in a single layer; sear undisturbed 60 seconds, then toss until just browned outside but still pink inside. Transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil. Stir-fry peppers and onion 2 minutes — they should stay crisp.
Push vegetables to one side. Add garlic, ginger, and black pepper to the cleared spot; toast 20 seconds, then toss everything together.
Return beef and any juices. Pour in sauce and toss until glossy and clinging, about 30 seconds. Serve immediately over rice.

recipes.title: Crispy Edge Egg Tacos
recipes.summary: A breakfast taco where the egg cooks directly onto the tortilla and crisps at the edges. Top with whatever cold thing is in the fridge.

ingredients.name: corn or flour tortillas (6 in / 15 cm)
shredded sharp cheddar or Oaxaca cheese

steps.text: Heat a wide nonstick skillet over medium. Melt a small knob of butter.
Lay one tortilla in the pan. Immediately crack an egg onto it. Use a spatula to gently push the white to the tortilla's edges so it crisps as it sets.
Sprinkle cheese on the white (not the yolk). Cook 90 seconds, until the bottom of the tortilla is golden and the egg white is set but the yolk is still runny.
Slide onto a plate. Repeat with remaining tortillas and eggs.
Top each taco with avocado, salsa, cilantro, a squeeze of lime, and flaky salt. Eat with your hands, over the sink.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Sea Salt Cookies
recipes.summary: Crisp edges, fudgy middle, puddles of chocolate, and a coarse-salt finish. Brown the butter and rest the dough overnight — both are non-negotiable.
recipes.prefaceNote: Resting the dough overnight is the single biggest flavor upgrade in this recipe. Skip it and you get a fine cookie. Don't skip it and you get the cookie.

ingredients.name: dark chocolate (70%), chopped into uneven shards (170 g)

steps.text: Brown butter in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat. Swirl until milk solids are deep amber and it smells nutty, 5–7 minutes. Scrape into a heatproof bowl. Cool 15 minutes until just barely warm.
Whisk both sugars into the cooled butter. Whisk in egg, yolk, and vanilla until smooth and glossy, 30 seconds.
Fold in flour, baking soda, and fine salt with a spatula until just combined. Fold in chocolate.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (24–36 hours is even better).
Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line two sheet pans with parchment. Scoop 3 tbsp portions, 3 in (7 cm) apart.
Bake one tray at a time, 10–12 minutes, until edges are deeply golden and the centers still look slightly underbaked.
Sprinkle each cookie with flaky salt the moment it leaves the oven. Cool 10 minutes on the tray before moving.

recipes.title: Frozen Mango Lassi
recipes.summary: Cold, thick, and barely sweet. Toasted cumin on top sounds weird and is correct.

steps.text: Toast cumin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking, until fragrant — 60 seconds. Cool, then crush coarsely.
Blend mango, yogurt, milk, honey, cardamom, and saffron until completely smooth, scraping the sides once.
Taste. Adjust with more milk if too thick or more honey if not sweet enough.
Pour into chilled glasses. Top with a small pinch of toasted cumin and a few extra saffron threads if you have them.

recipes.title: Furikake Popcorn
recipes.summary: Movie-night popcorn that's salty, savory, slightly briny, and impossible to stop eating.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter or vegan butter, melted

steps.text: Put oil and 3 kernels in a large heavy pot. Cover and heat over medium-high until all 3 kernels pop — that's the signal the oil is ready.
Add the rest of the kernels in an even layer. Cover, count to 30, then shake the pot every 5 seconds until popping slows to 2-second gaps. Pull off the heat.
Whisk melted butter, soy sauce, and sesame oil together.
Pour the butter mixture over the popcorn in stages, tossing between each addition so it coats evenly.
Shower with furikake and a pinch of flaky salt. Toss once more. Eat warm.

recipes.title: No-Knead Dutch Oven Bread
recipes.summary: One bowl, four ingredients, twelve hours. The Dutch oven traps steam and the loaf comes out with the kind of crust that crackles when you cut it.
recipes.prefaceNote: Total elapsed time is ~14 hours, but only 15 active minutes. Start it after dinner — bake it for breakfast.

steps.text: Whisk flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl. Pour in water and stir with a wooden spoon until you have a shaggy, sticky dough — no kneading.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a plate. Rest at room temperature 12–18 hours, until the surface is bubbly and the dough has doubled.

Turn the dough out onto a floured counter. Lightly flour your hands and fold the dough over itself a few times into a rough ball. Don't deflate it. Let it rest 30 minutes seam-side down on a square of floured parchment.
Meanwhile, put a 4–6 qt Dutch oven (lid on) in the oven and heat to 475°F (245°C) for 30 minutes.
Lift the parchment with the dough on it into the screaming-hot pot. Cover. Bake 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake another 10–15 minutes, until the crust is deep mahogany and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.
Lift out by the parchment and cool on a rack at least 45 minutes before slicing — the crumb is still setting.

recipes.epilogueNote: Day-old slices are the best toast you will ever make.
